title: Higher Executive Officer (HEO), moving up from Executive Officer
summary: Moving from EO to HEO: managing a team or leading a specialist area, and contributing to plans, budgets and advice. This route builds the people, delivery and money skills and the examples that HEO adverts ask for.

areas.label: Behaviours and evidence at HEO level
areas.why: Show Leadership, Managing a Quality Service and Delivering at Pace with real examples.

areas.label: Planning and delivering work
areas.why: Plan a work package, manage risks and report progress.

areas.label: Managing people
areas.why: Day-to-day management, feedback, performance and wellbeing.

areas.label: Budgets and value for money
areas.why: Understand a budget, forecasts and how public money is controlled.

areas.label: Governance, risk and compliance
areas.why: Know the rules your team works under and how decisions are recorded.

areas.label: Briefing and influencing
areas.why: Write clear advice and persuade colleagues without authority over them.

stages.label: Understand the next grade
stages.blurb: Read the HEO role profile and agree what evidence you need with your manager.

stages.label: Build the skills and evidence
stages.blurb: Build the management, delivery and money skills.

stages.label: Show it and apply
stages.blurb: Present your evidence in applications and interviews.

actions.label: Read two HEO adverts and their role profiles
actions.detail: Note the Behaviours, the size of team or budget, and the Success Profile elements assessed (ability, technical, experience).

actions.label: Ask about acting up or a temporary promotion
actions.detail: Deputise for your manager for a period, or lead a project, so you have first-hand HEO evidence.

actions.label: Write six examples at HEO level
actions.detail: Cover leading people, delivering a piece of work, improving a process, handling a difficult situation, working across teams and using data.

actions.label: Take on supervising or coaching one person
actions.detail: Agree objectives, give regular feedback and keep notes of what changed as a result.

actions.label: Practise a panel interview out loud
actions.detail: Include a short presentation if the advert asks for one. Time yourself.

apply.label: Apply for HEO vacancies
apply.detail: Apply to HEO roles as they appear. Many are competitions open to people already in the Civil Service. Ask for feedback after every result and use it to improve your next application.
